The live page confirms the WG-SS is a 6-domain functioning measure developed and maintained by the Washington Group on Disability Statistics for use in censuses and surveys. It describes the six domains (seeing, hearing, mobility, cognition, self-care, communication are implicit in "six basic, universal actions") and references the ICF framework. The page also explicitly mentions the WG/UNICEF Child Functioning Module (CFM) as a separate tool for children, consistent with the recorded notes explaining why WG-SS applies to adults only. No contradictions detected with the recorded status, source attribution, or conceptual description.

The live page confirms all recorded details: publication date 30 June 2026, source attribution to Government Digital Service, DSIT, and DCMS, the 11 top-level categories in the exact order recorded, and the explicit statements that "Gender or sexual identity" is "intentionally not expanded for now" and "Ethnicity" is "intentionally omitted for now". The page structure and hierarchy of categories, sub-categories, and risk factors matches the recorded description.

The live page confirms all key recorded metadata: Department for Education as source, published 12 September 2018, last updated 23 April 2019, and the 5 skill domains listed verbatim ("communicating", "handling information and content", "transacting", "problem-solving", "being safe and legal online"). The live page now prominently states "This harmonised standard is under development" and indicates the standard is "currently reviewing and updating," whereas the recorded status is "current" with a note to "treat as current, not archived." The recorded notes mention active review since March 2022 but explicitly instruct to keep using this standard for existing collections until review concludes. The live page's emphasis on "under development" warrants verification of whether the status designation should be reconsidered.

The live page states "This harmonised standard is under development following the Inclusive Data Taskforce recommendations" and indicates it is "a priority topic" for review. The recorded status is "current" and notes mention draft revised questions expected by 2025, but the page now explicitly flags the standard as under active development, which may represent a material change in status that should be verified directly.

The live page confirms all key recorded details: it states plainly "There is not currently a harmonised standard for collecting data on sex," references Census 2021/2022 historical categories for context only, describes active work on two distinct approaches (biological sex and certificated sex), confirms cognitive/usability testing is underway, and states new guidance is expected in Summer 2026. The April 2025 Supreme Court ruling on sex under the Equality Act 2010 is also referenced. The source remains ONS/GSS Harmonisation Team with status "under-review" accurately reflecting active development work.

The live page confirms the archived status with the explicit notice: "Following the publication of an updated GSS Harmonisation workplan in December 2024, this guidance is outdated and has been archived." The publication date of 16 July 2020 and source ownership (GSS Harmonisation Team) match the recorded metadata. The response options shown ("Yes", "No, enter gender identity", "Prefer not to say") match the recorded summary. The age specification (16 and over) with no under-16 provision stated aligns with the recorded notes. No contradictions detected.

The live page confirms all key recorded details: publication date 17 April 2019, owner GSS Harmonisation Team, status as current guidance, and the self-completion mode with the exact five options listed (Heterosexual or Straight, Gay or Lesbian, Bisexual, Other, Prefer not to say). The page explicitly warns against altering wording or option order to maintain comparability with ONS benchmarks, and confirms the standard applies to respondents aged 16 and over, all matching the recorded notes.

The live page confirms all key recorded details: publication date is 5 June 2020, owner is GSS Harmonisation Team, status appears current with no under-review notice, the five response options (Very good, Good, Fair, Bad, Very bad) match exactly, the EU-SILC harmonisation and Minimum European Health Module equivalence are stated, and the explicit warning "This question is a subjective measure and should not be asked by proxy" is present. The live page confirms all key recorded details: publication date 19 May 2020, GSS Harmonisation Team ownership, the four question items with their exact wording, 0-10 numeric response scale for all items, and explicit documentation that the anxiety item has different anchor wording ("0 is not at all anxious" vs "0 is not at all" for others) and separate severity bands. The page also confirms "these questions are used together, in the order they are presented" and references the "ONS4" terminology, supporting the recorded modelling notes about why this is kept as a single entry despite the anxiety item's divergent characteristics.

The live page text confirms the recorded status and purpose. The page lists the same six differently-worded pregnancy screening questions referenced in the notes (Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, Health Survey for England questionnaire and nurse visit, National Survey for Wales, Scottish Health Survey, Taking Part Survey), confirming the inconsistency the recorded entry describes. The recorded source_published date is "2018-02-01" (February 2018), but the live page shows "Publication date: 17 April 2019". The recorded notes reference the document as "Version 1.0, ONS, February 2018" and "unrevised since February 2018", but the live page indicates April 2019 as the publication date. This discrepancy warrants human verification to determine which date is correct and whether the document or its hosting has actually been updated.

The live page confirms all key recorded details: the standard is still marked "under development" (supporting the "under-review" status), the publication date remains 16 March 2022, it was developed by ONS and MoD and adopted by GSS, and the Office for Veterans' Affairs concerns about the Reserve armed forces response categories are prominently displayed with the exact same wording. The live page shows the standard now includes eight recommended questions to measure socio-economic background (School type, Free school meals, Employee/self-employed/not working, Number of employees in two versions, Supervisor status, Parental occupation, Parental qualification), which is substantially different from the recorded notes that focus primarily on just two retrospective questions about parental occupation and qualification. The recorded entry does not mention school type, free school meals, employment status, or supervisor status questions.

The live page confirms all key recorded details: publication date 9 June 2020, owner GSS Harmonisation Team, status statement "It is expected that the internet access harmonised standard will be reviewed in the coming years" and "this standard has not been further developed or updated since" (2022), mode restriction warning about internet-based self-administered surveys, spontaneous "Don't know" responses, no Welsh-language version, and the two primary questions (household internet access: Yes/No with spontaneous Don't know; individual use: Yes/No with spontaneous Don't know). The recorded values_or_items_summary lists five response options ("Often or Always", "Some of the time", "Occasionally", "Hardly ever", "Never"), but the live page shows the adult measure's fourth question (direct loneliness measure) has these same five options, while the first three adult questions use only three options ("Hardly ever or never", "Some of the time", "Often"). The recorded summary appears to reflect only one subset of the response sets, and the live page reveals a more complex picture with different questions having different response scales that wasn't clearly captured in the recorded summary.

The live page confirms all key recorded details: publication date of 13 July 2021, status as "under development" (recorded as under-review), GSS Harmonisation Team ownership, OECD definition of social capital, the four domains (personal relationships, social network support, civic engagement, trust/cooperative norms), and all six component questions with their exact wording and response scales match what was noted in the recorded entry. The live page confirms all key recorded details: published by MHCLG on 30 October 2025, status is current (stated as "updates the English indices of deprivation 2019"), and covers Lower-layer Super Output Areas. The page confirms the 7 weighted domains structure via the "Domains of deprivation" file listing and references to income, employment, education, health, crime, housing/services, and living environment dimensions. The live page confirms SIMD 2020v2 remains the current published version with data for 6,976 data zones across seven domains (income, employment, education, health, access to services, crime, and housing). The page explicitly states the 2020v2 revision affected only income domain ranks and overall SIMD ranks due to a DWP problem, and advises that "SIMD 2020v2 ranks should now be used when carrying out any analyses." No mention of SIMD 2026 appears on this live page, and the status as "current" remains accurate as of the review date.

The live page confirms WIMD 2025 is current, published 27 November 2025, and maintained by Welsh Government. The page structure, publication date, and status all align with what's recorded. No inconsistencies detected in the visible content.

The live page confirms all key recorded facts: NIMDM 2017 published 23 November 2017 by NISRA, ranks 890 Super Output Areas, covers 7 distinct domains of deprivation, and no newer edition is evident. The page title, source, publication date, and domain count all match the recorded data.

The live page shows a last update of 31 March 2026 (not 6 March 2025 as recorded for source_published), and describes a substantive methodology change: the 2021 RUC now uses only three simplified OA categories ("Urban", "Larger rural settlement", "Smaller rural settlement") rather than six, with "Relative access" (not "Sparsity") dividing each into "Nearer" or "Further" classes. The recorded values_or_items_summary lists the correct six items derived from these three × two subdivisions, but the methodology description in the notes should be verified against the live page's explicit statement that the 2021 version "streamlines the taxonomy" and represents improvements over 2011, including replacing "Sparsity" with "Relative access." A human should confirm whether the recorded notes accurately capture these methodology details.

The live page confirms all key details: it is published by GeoDS in partnership with ONS, describes the classification as hierarchical geodemographic across the UK with 8 supergroups, 21 groups, and 52 sub-groups, version 3.2 released January 2025, and covers England, Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland. The note about pen portrait name changes (4b1 and 8b3) aligns with the recorded understanding that actual names live in accompanying documents. No discrepancies detected.

The live page confirms all key recorded facts: OAs are the lowest level with "usually resident population between 100 and 625 persons"; LSOAs are "made up of groups of Output Areas (OAs)" with "usually resident population between 1,000 and 3,000 persons"; MSOAs are "made up of groups of Lower layer Super Output Areas (LSOAs)" with "usually resident population between 5,000 and 15,000 persons." The hierarchical nesting structure and population thresholds match the recorded information. The page also notes Scotland and Northern Ireland have separate census arrangements, consistent with the recorded notes about different naming conventions. No contradictions or material drift detected.
